help.title: About Inspections
help.overview: An inspection is a scheduled visit to a unit: type, status, inspector, dates, findings, media, and an optional structured checklist. It is quality / handover evidence. It is not a reservation, not a snag list (findings often become snags later), and not a sale handover package.

sections.title: What an inspection holds
items: Unit (required). The card also shows floor, inspector, inspection date, and next inspection date.
Type: initial, follow-up, final, routine, complaint, pre-sale, post-sale.
Status: scheduled → in progress → completed, or cancelled / rescheduled.
Optional checklist template plus the live item rows copied onto this inspection (name, importance, completed).
Findings by category (structural, electrical, plumbing, HVAC, safety, cosmetic, other) with notes, media, severity, and optional resolved-at.
Cancellation reason and cancelled-at when you cancel a scheduled visit.

sections.title: Structured checklist
sections.body: Checklist items are structured rows, not a JSON blob. The template defines the items; ticks and completion live on the inspection.
items: Attach a company template from Tenancy → Configurations → Inspection checklists.
Open inspections live-sync when that template’s items change: new items appear, renamed items update, removed incomplete items drop.
If you already ticked an item and it is later removed from the template, the inspection keeps that row as retained so the tick is not lost.
Switching template re-merges from the new list and keeps completed rows that no longer match.
On the sheet, the Checklist Template card has a reference link that opens the template sheet.
Archived templates disappear from the picker; an inspection that already uses one keeps syncing from it while still open.

sections.title: Actions
items: Cancel scheduled — only while status is scheduled; stores a reason and timestamp. You cannot cancel a completed inspection.
Update checklist — tick or untick live items from the row, card, or sheet menu while the inspection is open.
Complete — status cannot become completed until every live (non-retained) checklist item is ticked. Inspections with no checklist have no such gate.
Reschedule by setting status to rescheduled and a new date — that is not a new inspection document unless you create one.

sections.title: Freeze after close
items: Completed and cancelled inspections stop syncing from the template and reject further checklist toggles.
The snapshot on that inspection is the record of what was checked at close.

sections.title: On this page
items: Create an inspection against a unit. Filter by project, edifice, floor, unit, type, status, and follow-up required.
Cards show unit, inspector, inspection date, and next inspection date. Open the sheet for findings, media, and the checklist.
Company-wide list from Real Estate → Inspections; from a unit, the list can be scoped to that unit.

sections.title: How it behaves
items: An inspection never changes unit commercial status.
It is not a snag: open defects that need a trade and an assignee belong on Snags.
It is not a modification request: client-asked changes go through architect / engineer / CEO / finance / delivery there.
It is not a handover package: sale handover checklists stack by project / edifice / floor / unit and tick on the sale.

sections.title: Related records
items: Unit (and thus floor / edifice / project).
Inspection checklists (Tenancy → Configurations) — the reusable templates you attach here.
Follow-on: Snags, Modification requests, Sale handover.
